notes:
[IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20 — working tree only, not committed] Repaired the unreachable grain guard in create_data_gaps_table and closed the function's zero-test gap. 2 files.

(1) THE FIX. Step 6 now builds an explicit pre-dedup frame (data_gaps_prededup). GUARD (A) counts THAT frame (rows vs distinct country_key) and raises ValueError naming the duplicated key(s) plus an upstream fix hint, BEFORE write_tbl is ever called. dropDuplicates(["country_key"]) moved below it as belt-and-braces, and the original post-dedup check is retained as GUARD (B) with a corrected message. Message text differentiated ('upstream of the dedup' vs 'after dedup') so a failure identifies which guard fired.

(2) COMMENTS CORRECTED — this is the part that let the defect survive two tasks. (A)'s comment now states why the check must run pre-dedup, and that the only fan-out vector in steps 1-5 is gold_dim_country losing country_key uniqueness (every other input is a DISTINCT or GROUP BY on country_key). (B)'s comment now says PLAINLY that it is unreachable from any input by design and defends only a dedup-key regression to a role-grained key — it no longer claims to catch upstream fan-out.

(3) BEFORE/AFTER RUN BOTH WAYS, EXPLICITLY. With HEAD's pre-fix notebook restored in place (byte-swapped in, then restored and sha256-verified identical afterwards — no git add/stash, no commit), the two new guard tests FAILED: 'DID NOT RAISE ValueError' and 'create_data_gaps_table did not raise on a fanned-out grain' (2 failed, 7 passed). With the fix in place all 9 PASS. The tests are therefore load-bearing rather than vacuous — the exact check whose absence let the original guard ship inert.

(4) NINE TESTS ADDED to tests/test_data_quality.py.
  TestDataGapsGrainGuard — a duplicate gold_dim_country row raises; the message names the key and the 5-rows-for-4-countries counts; the fan-out is caught BEFORE anything is written.
  TestDataGapsTable — one row per country including a dual-role country carrying both role flags; the written table's grain; SUM(spend_eur) == fact_procurement total (200.0, i.e. the +23.7% regression); supplier-HQ-only spend semantics (production-only country = 0.0 / 0 txns — task-074 defect #2); placeholder exclusion; coverage flags and data_status across all four statuses (EPI abbrev filter, WGI six-dimension + value-not-null rules); and summary counts/percentages with an assertion that no '%' metric exceeds 100 — task-071's 158.33% regression.

HARNESS runs the notebook's OWN function via load_notebook_functions. Inputs registered as global temp views with DB injected as 'global_temp' (no metastore db, no on-disk warehouse, no Delta writer); write_tbl stubbed and passed in by the caller so it stays inspectable after the raise; WGI_REQUIRED_INDICATORS read from the notebook source by ast rather than restated; results materialized to dicts to avoid lazy re-evaluation against a later test's views and to sidestep the Row/tuple hazard — no column aliased 'count' (the notebook's new dup-key probe aliases 'n').

SELF-REVIEW: notebook re-parsed with ast (OK); cell delimiters unchanged vs HEAD (23 '# CELL', 1 '# PARAMETERS CELL'); no new Delta-written column names; ANSI stays off via conftest's session fixture; grep with positive control confirms src/transformations/ holds NO mirror of create_data_gaps_table (only a prose cross-reference in supply_risk.py), so no parity side to update; grep with positive control confirms no docs/ file cites the guard text, and data_quality_architecture.md was left untouched per the parallel-agent constraint. Full suite: 349 passed in 61s (340 + 9).
title: task-074's gold_data_gaps grain guard is unreachable — it sits below the dropDuplicates that makes it a tautology
description:
DEMONSTRATED, NOT INFERRED — and found independently twice: task-074's own verify-agent flagged it as minor issue #2, and phase-level verification re-derived it 2026-08-20 and escalated it.

In silver_to_gold.Notebook's create_data_gaps_table the guard reads:

    data_gaps = ( ... ).dropDuplicates(["country_key"])
    row_total = data_gaps.count()
    country_total = data_gaps.select("country_key").distinct().count()
    if row_total != country_total: raise ValueError("gold_data_gaps grain violation: ...")

After dropDuplicates on country_key those counts are equal by construction, so the ValueError cannot be raised from any input.

Probe: a local[1] SparkSession (spark.sql.ansi.enabled=false) executing the notebook's own function via load_notebook_functions, with a gold_dim_country fixture carrying TWO rows for country_key 'DE'. The guard did not fire; the duplicate was silently collapsed to one arbitrary surviving row — the same 'kept an ARBITRARY row per key' hazard the notebook already warns about at L691.

So the guard defends only against someone re-editing the dedup key back to (country_key, country_role) — worth having — but NOT against the upstream fan-out its own comment claims to catch.

Suggested fix: evaluate the guard on the PRE-DEDUP frame (the gaps_detail.join(spend_by_country, ...) result) so an upstream fan-out raises, keeping dropDuplicates below it as belt-and-braces. Add a regression test feeding a duplicated gold_dim_country row and asserting ValueError — today no test covers the guard's firing path, which is exactly how it shipped inert.

NOT a correctness defect in the shipped table: gold_data_gaps is genuinely one row per country today (12 rows / 12 countries live; 11/11 local assertions green including SUM(spend_eur) reconciling to fact_procurement exactly). This is hardening the defence, not fixing a live inflation.

ABSORBS the standing observation that create_data_gaps_table has zero regression tests despite two consecutive grain defects (task-071, task-074).
acceptanceCriteria: The guard is moved (or a second guard added) so it evaluates a population that CAN violate the invariant — demonstrated by a test that makes it raise.
A regression test feeds a duplicated gold_dim_country row and asserts ValueError; it must FAIL against today's code and pass after the fix (state both results).
The guard's comment is corrected so it no longer claims to catch a failure mode it cannot see.
Coverage is added for create_data_gaps_table's core invariants (one row per country; SUM(spend_eur) == fact total), closing the zero-test gap two grain defects were shipped through.

issues.description: Guard B's comment names a trigger it cannot actually reach: regressing the dedup key to ['country_key','is_production'] in a /tmp copy and feeding the fan-out fixture, guard A raised first so B never evaluated; on a clean population B is unreachable for any dedup key because A already guarantees the pre-dedup frame is country-unique and dropDuplicates never adds rows. B in fact defends only against the dedup step being replaced by something row-multiplying. The comment's central corrective claim ('unreachable from any input — that is deliberate') is accurate and criterion 3 is met; only the illustrative (country_key, country_role) scenario is imprecise.

Deploy-time behaviour change worth knowing before the next Fabric run: guard A converts a previously silent collapse into a hard pipeline halt, so a live gold_dim_country carrying duplicate country_key rows would now stop silver_to_gold instead of quietly picking an arbitrary row. Structurally prevented in source (gold_dim_country is row_number().over(partitionBy('country_key')) filtered to rn==1 at L701-712), but that is a code-level guarantee, not a live measurement.

test_spend_is_supplier_hq_spend_only's docstring frames the production-only-country assertion as pinning task-074 defect #2, but that defect's signature was a DUAL-role country's 'Production' row carrying supplier-HQ spend; the assertion pins the supplier-HQ spend definition rather than that specific regression. The regression is genuinely pinned elsewhere, so coverage is complete — only the docstring's attribution is generous.

verification_history.notes:
PASS on independent re-derivation. Every load-bearing claim was re-run with the verifier's OWN fixture (France/India/Norway/placeholder, spend 250.0/125.5/75.25/300.0, fact total 750.75), never the implementer's — and the working tree was NEVER modified. HEAD's pre-fix notebook was extracted to /tmp and driven through the repo's own load_notebook_functions(path, ...), which takes the notebook path as a parameter — cleaner than the implementer's in-place byte-swap. git diff --numstat byte-identical before and after verification.

(1) BEFORE/AFTER REPRODUCED TWO WAYS. Direct probe: against HEAD's notebook a duplicated gold_dim_country row raised NOTHING, write_tbl was called for both tables, and the duplicate was silently collapsed to 3 rows — the inert guard confirmed. Against the working tree the same input raised ValueError 'gold_data_gaps grain violation upstream of the dedup: 4 rows for 3 distinct countries. Duplicated country_key(s): [102]' and write_tbl was called ZERO times (captured in a caller-owned dict so the 'nothing written' assertion cannot be vacuous). Test-suite probe: a pytest plugin repointed GOLD_NOTEBOOK at the /tmp HEAD copy — 2 failed ('DID NOT RAISE ValueError'), 7 passed; against the fix all 9 pass. The stated before/after is exactly right and the two guard tests are load-bearing rather than shape-fitting.

(2) GUARD A REACHABLE AND CORRECTLY ORDERED. Raises on fan-out, names the duplicated key, raises before any write, and does NOT fire on a correct population.

(3) OUTPUT UNCHANGED — the central safety claim. On a clean population HEAD and the fix produce identical results: 3 rows / 3 distinct country_keys, SUM(spend_eur) 750.75 == fact total exactly, identical per-country payload (spend, transaction_count, is_supplier_hq, is_production, data_status), identical summary metrics, and no '%' metric above 100 in either. Hardening, not a behaviour change on valid data.

(4) TESTS ARE REAL COVERAGE. They execute the notebook's own function — proved empirically, since swapping the source file flipped the outcomes. WGI_REQUIRED_INDICATORS is injected by reading it from the notebook via ast rather than restated; results materialize to dicts so a later view replacement cannot re-evaluate them (also dodging the Row/tuple hazard); _run_create_data_gaps re-registers all five views per call, so tests are order-independent. task-071 (>100% metric) pinned by an explicit over_100 sweep plus EPI Coverage == 50.0; task-074 pinned by the dual-role country being ONE row with both flags, SUM == fact total, and production-only == 0.0 / 0 txns.

(5) NOTEBOOK INTEGRITY. ast.parse clean on both versions. Delimiters unchanged vs HEAD: 23 '# CELL', 1 '# PARAMETERS CELL', 23 '# MARKDOWN'. All four diff hunks fall inside create_data_gaps_table; the written select block is untouched, so no column names changed and no Delta-illegal name introduced. The new dup-key probe aliases 'n', not 'count'. (Pre-existing and OUTSIDE this diff: alias("count") at L2109/L2118 and 'COUNT(*) as count' at L4228 — all display-only via .show()/orderBy, never attribute-read, so not a live instance of the Row/tuple hazard.)

(6) SUITE: 349 passed in 60.5s, confirmed independently. Test-def count 45 -> 54 = +9, matching 340 + 9.

(7) SCOPE. docs/data_quality_architecture.md is task-077's — verified rather than taken on trust (task-077 Finished, verification pass, files_affected exactly that one file). No undeclared files.

(8) CONSISTENCY, every negative finding positive-controlled in the same command: src/ holds no mirror of create_data_gaps_table (control: same grep shape returns real defs from supply_risk.py), so no parity side to update. No docs/ file cites the guard wording (control: gold_data_gaps found in data_quality_framework.md). The notebook comment's cross-reference to TestDataGapsGrainGuard resolves. No TODO/FIXME introduced (control: the same grep finds real 'pragma: no cover'/'noqa' markers).

(9) PATTERN FIT. The pre-dedup count-then-raise idiom already exists in this notebook at L2552 for the WGI weight join, with the same 'assert it anyway, because the failure is silent and the fix is upstream' rationale. Guard A follows an established in-repo pattern.

No Fabric measurement attempted or claimed. The change is pure DataFrame logic with no Delta or lakehouse dependency — exactly the layer that is locally executable, and it was executed.
